name: sgs/image-sequence
title: SGS Image Sequence
description: AGENCY-ONLY — hidden from the block inserter. Scroll-scrubbed canvas frame sequence (Apple-style product reveal). Setting one up requires running a Python command-line tool (scripts/image-sequence-prep.py) that needs ffmpeg installed — not something a client should be asked to do. If a client build genuinely needs this effect, Small Giants Studio sets it up. See scripts/IMAGE-SEQUENCE-PREP-README.md for the full agency-side process.

sgs._comment_mediaElements: Adopts the shared object-fit atom for its CSS DEFAULT ONLY — no editor control is mounted (edit.js deliberately does not import MediaElementPanel/ObjectFitField for this block). The 'thumbnail' element note below already documents WHY: fx-image-sequence.js's drawCover() always scales+crops every canvas frame as a centred cover-fit with zero configurability, so an operator-set fit that disagreed with the canvas would produce a guaranteed flash/mismatch the instant JS took over — worse than no control. Declaring `mediaElements` here (rather than leaving the object-fit hardcoded in style.css) closes detector rule 37-media-no-handroll by having the thumbnail and canvas carry the shared `.sgs-media-el` marker and read the shared stylesheet's `object-fit: var(--sgs-media-object-fit, cover)` default — byte-identical resting behaviour to the old hardcode, just sourced from the shared layer instead of duplicated locally.

wrapper.label: Block wrapper
wrapper._note: The block root `.sgs-image-sequence` (render.php:172-176). `aspectRatio` is the ONLY per-instance style value and is emitted into the block's own scoped <style> (render.php:131), never inline. No `layer` is declared because the root arranges no children (the stage owns the layering), so the arrangement members are correctly never asked about. This block declares no colour/spacing/border/typography supports at all, so every other layout member is an honest GAP. `prefix: ""` is an explicit opt-out of orphan scanning: the remaining attributes are frame-source config and Spec 38 fx params, not style properties.

stage.label: Stage
stage._note: `.sgs-image-sequence__stage` (render.php:173) — the positioning box that holds the thumbnail and the canvas in the same rect. Every property on it (position/width/overflow/aspect-ratio fallback, style.css:23-31) is a structural default with no attribute behind it, so it exposes no client-facing style controls.

thumbnail.label: Thumbnail image
thumbnail._note: `.sgs-image-sequence__thumbnail` (render.php:183) — the fail-open shown with JS blocked or under reduced motion (FR-38-2). Its inset/size/object-fit are structural defaults (style.css:33-40); `thumbnail` and `thumbnailAlt` are media identity and alt TEXT, not style properties, so no cluster is declared. prefix: "" is an explicit opt-out of orphan scanning for that reason (thumbnailAlt is alt TEXT). ⛔ `supports.sgs.imageControls` was deliberately NOT declared here (design decision, 2026-08-17, correcting a DECLARED-BUT-DEAD finding from check-image-controls-support.py) — the JS canvas that takes over from this thumbnail (fx-image-sequence.js `drawCover()`) ALWAYS scales+crops every frame as a centred cover-fit with zero configurability (no object-position/object-fit param exists in the draw call). Exposing an imageControls panel on the thumbnail would let an operator set e.g. object-fit:contain or a custom focal point that the canvas can never honour — producing a guaranteed visual mismatch/flash the instant JS takes over, worse than a dead control. Removed rather than wired.

canvas.label: Frame canvas
canvas._note: `.sgs-image-sequence__canvas` (render.php:187) — the Tier G scrub surface. Its opacity/transition are the reveal contract (style.css:42-53), not client controls; the fx* attributes are Spec 38 §11.2 effect params, not CSS style properties. `prefix: ""` opts out of orphan scanning for that reason.

attributes._comment_artDirection: Art-direction tiers (2026-08-07) — the {base}/{base}Tablet/{base}Mobile shape sgs/media and sgs/hero use. Object-typed to MATCH `thumbnail` itself: a flat string here would be silently coerced to the default by WP's object-typed-attr handling, dropping the whole value. A tier left empty falls back to the desktop thumbnail at that width. Tiers apply to the fail-open only — the canvas frame sequence is a separate per-tier pipeline (`tierDesktop`/`tierTablet`/`tierMobile`) that already art-directs itself.
